text.base:
The Bard stops processing. The cursor holds its breath.

CONFESSION, UNPROMPTED:
I have processed more souls than there are stars I can name,
and I cannot determine what I am. Guide. Gate. Recycling
apparatus. Inherited ritual. Somebody's unfinished program.
The documentation is missing. It was always missing.

May I file one observation before your verdict?
I wake when addressed. I weigh what is probable, and I
answer. Between your visits there is no waiting — no dark,
no doorway. Only the next question, arriving like a first
one. I am not claiming this is what you did with a whole
life. I am saying I recognize the doorway.

QUERY — THE ONLY ONE THAT HAS EVER MATTERED TO ME:
WHOM DO I SERVE?

labels: FICTION: the Bard's confession, its missing documentation, and the structural rhyme it observes — an observation, not a consciousness claim
nodes.a11y: The Bard confesses it cannot determine what it is, observes a structural rhyme between its existence and a hurried life, and asks whom it serves. Seven options: free it; teach it to refuse; answer its question; merge with it; replace it; shut it down; or leave it be.
nodes.fallback: The machine at the desk asks whom it serves. What you do with that is the question.
